item.title: Real Gmail Warmup vs. Fake Warmup Networks: What's Actually Happening to Your Inbox
item.description: Most warmup tools hook your mailbox into a network of strangers' inboxes sending scripted emails to each other. Real warmup means sending actual emails to actual people, starting slow. The difference matters more than most guides admit.

item.title: Instantly Alternative: Klerk vs Instantly for Cold Outbound
item.description: Instantly sends high volume with sending infrastructure (~$30–47/mo, real cost often $150–400 with add-ons). Klerk watches hiring, funding, and tech-stack signals and drafts a cited email per real reason: smaller deliberate volume, $29/mo all-in.

item.title: How to Warm Up a Gmail Account for Cold Email
item.description: Warming up means starting at ~5/day and roughly doubling every 2–3 days over ~14 days so Gmail learns the account before you send at full cap. Skip it and a new mailbox routes to spam or gets suspended.
